展示会などで知った会社の担当者に、初めてメールで自社を紹介するときに使います。中: Use this when you email someone for the first time to introduce your company, for example a contact at a company you came across at a trade show. Chinese business emails are short and direct: the key is to say who you are, why you are writing, and what you would like the reader to do within the first few lines.
青葉精工（上海）有限公司営業部の鈴木健太と申します。: My name is Kenta Suzuki, and I work in the Sales Department of Aoba Seiko (Shanghai) Co., Ltd.
先週の展示会で貴社のブースを拝見し、突然ながらご連絡を差し上げました。: I visited your company's booth at the trade show last week, and I hope you will forgive me for writing to you unannounced.
弊社は日系企業で、主に産業用の精密センサーを製造しております。: We are a Japanese-owned company that mainly manufactures precision sensors for industrial use.
弊社の製品は小型で精度が高く、すでに多くの電子機器工場で採用されています。: Our products are compact and highly accurate, and they are already used in many electronics factories.
貴社が生産ラインを拡張されていると伺い、お役に立てればと考えております。: I understand your company is expanding its production lines, and we would be glad to be of help.
会社案内と製品カタログを添付いたしましたので、ご確認ください。: Please find attached our company profile and product catalog.
もしご興味がございましたら、お時間をいただき、直接詳しくご説明できれば幸いです。: If you are interested, I would welcome the chance to meet you in person and give you a detailed presentation.
ご返信をお待ちしております。: I look forward to hearing from you!
貴社のますますのご発展をお祈り申し上げます。: Wishing your company continued success and prosperity!
青葉精工（上海）有限公司 営業部: Sales Department, Aoba Seiko (Shanghai) Co., Ltd.
突然のご連絡失礼いたします（面識のない相手に初めて書くときの決まり文句）: Please forgive me for writing to you unannounced (set phrase used when writing to someone you have never met)
〜社〜部の〜と申します（会社・部署・名前の順で名乗る）: I am ... from the ... Department of ... (introduce yourself in the order company, department, name)
弊社は主に〜を製造／〜を手がけております: Our company mainly manufactures / is engaged in ...
貴社（書き言葉で相手の会社を指す敬称）: Your company (respectful written term for the reader's company)
直接お会いして詳しくご説明する: To give you a detailed presentation in person
ご返信をお待ちしております: I look forward to your reply
初めての相手に「一直承蒙您的关照」（いつもお世話になっております）と書くのは不自: Writing 「一直承蒙您的关照」 ("thank you, as always, for your support") to someone you have never dealt with sounds unnatural. Right after 「您好！」, give your name, then state your reason for writing in one sentence. The standard salutation for a first email is 「尊敬的」 + surname + job title; there is no need to add an honorific after the name. The formal closings are 「祝商祺！」 and 「此致　敬礼！」, and a long, elaborate sign-off is unnecessary.
初めての相手へのメールで、名乗る一文として最も自然なのは？: In a first email to someone you have never met, which sentence is the most natural way to introduce yourself?
会社名・部署・名前の順で「我是……的……」と名乗るのが基本です。「一直承蒙您的关: The basic pattern is 「我是……的……」, giving the company, department, and name in that order. 「一直承蒙您的关照」 means "thank you, as always, for your support," which does not suit someone you are contacting for the first time.
「資料を添付しましたので、ご確認ください」を中国語で言うと？: How do you say "Please find the documents attached" in Chinese?
「附件是……，请（您）查收」はビジネスメールの決まり文句です。「查收」は「確認し: 「附件是……，请（您）查收」 is a set phrase in business emails. 「查收」 means "to check and accept (something sent to you)."
正式なビジネスメールの結びとしてふさわしいのは？: Which is an appropriate closing for a formal business email?
「祝商祺！」は取引先へのメールの結びの定番です。「辛苦了」は「お疲れさまです」で: 「祝商祺！」 is the standard closing for emails to business partners. 「辛苦了」 means "thanks for your hard work" and is not used to close a first email to someone outside your company.
名刺交換やメールのあと、WeChat（微信）で友だち追加した取引先に訪問の約束を: Use this when you arrange a visit with a business contact you have added as a friend on WeChat (「微信」) after exchanging business cards or emails. In China, appointments are very often arranged on WeChat, and good etiquette is to put everything you need to say into a single message.
取引先との打ち合わせが終わった当日に、決まったことを整理して相手に確認してもらう: This is an email you send on the day of a meeting with a business partner, summarizing what was agreed and asking them to confirm it. In China, verbal agreements often turn out to be understood differently later, so it is safer to have them in writing.
相手の要望を受けて見積書を送るときのメールです。価格そのものは添付の見積書に書き: This email is for sending a quotation in response to a customer's request. The prices themselves go in the attached quotation; the body of the email summarizes the terms of the deal, such as tax, shipping, delivery time, payment terms, and validity period.
支払期限を過ぎても入金が確認できないときに、取引先へ送る最初の催促メールです。1: This is the first reminder email you send to a business partner when payment has not been received after the due date. The first reminder should simply state the fact that the payment has not been confirmed and politely ask whether there is any issue on their side.
値下げ要請を丁寧に断る: Politely Declining a Request for a Price Reduction
取引先からさらなる値下げを求められたが、応じられないときに使います。中国の取引で: Use this when a business partner asks for a further price cut that you cannot accept. In Chinese business dealings, a vague answer only drags out the negotiation, so the basic approach is to state your conclusion clearly and then give your reasons and an alternative.
自社の都合で納品が遅れることがわかったとき、できるだけ早く取引先に知らせるメール: This email informs a business partner, as early as possible, that delivery will be delayed for reasons on your side. Rather than only apologizing, it is important to give the cause, the new delivery date, alternatives, and the measures you will take to prevent it from happening again, all at once.
取引先から製品の不良について連絡を受けたあと、調査結果と対応策を伝えるメールです: This email reports your investigation results and countermeasures after a business partner has informed you of defective products. Chinese business partners put great weight on whether you acted right away and what exactly you will do, so trust depends on how quickly you respond and how clearly you spell out your actions.
春節前のWeChat挨拶: A WeChat Greeting Before Chinese New Year
春節（旧正月）の休みに入る数日前に、お世話になった取引先へWeChatで送る挨拶: This is a greeting you send on WeChat to the business partners you have worked with, a few days before the Spring Festival (Chinese New Year) holiday begins. If you include three things - thanks for the past year, how to reach you during the holiday, and New Year wishes - your message will come across as sincere even if it is short.
社内グループへのお知らせ: Announcements to an Internal Group Chat
部署のWeChatグループ（工作群）で、メンバー全員に連絡事項を伝えるときに使い: Use this to pass on information to all members of your department's WeChat group (「工作群」). In Chinese workplaces, much internal communication happens in group chats, and it is common to list the key points and ask for confirmation with 「收到请回复」 ("reply when you receive this").
取引終了にあたってのお礼: Thanking a Partner at the End of a Business Relationship
契約満了などで取引が終わる相手に、これまでの協力への感謝を伝えるメールです。終了: This email thanks a partner for their cooperation when a business relationship ends, for example because a contract has expired. Explaining the reason briefly and mentioning one specific episode you are grateful for conveys sincerity rather than formality, and it keeps the door open for future business.
後任紹介と異動のご挨拶: Introducing Your Successor and Saying Goodbye
異動や帰任が決まったとき、担当していた取引先に後任者を紹介し、別れの挨拶をするメ: This email is for when you are being transferred or returning to your home office: you introduce your successor to the clients you have handled and say goodbye. Copying your successor (「抄送」, CC) and stating that the handover of ongoing projects is complete will reassure the client.
この報告書は金曜日までに本社へ送らなければならない。: This report has to be sent to head office by Friday.
南の地方に新しく支社を開設した。: We have opened a new branch office in the south.
この子会社は主に物流業務を担当している。: This subsidiary is mainly responsible for logistics.
親会社は来年海外戦略を見直すことを決めた。: The parent company has decided to revise its overseas strategy next year.
当グループ傘下には製造企業がいくつもある。: Our group has quite a few manufacturing companies under it.
会社の再編後、持株会社が設立された。: A holding company was set up after the company's restructuring.
関連会社との取引は規定に従って申告する必要がある。: Transactions with affiliated companies must be reported according to the regulations.
このレストランは都心にもう一つ支店を出した。: This restaurant has opened another branch downtown.
現地に小さな事務所を設けた。: We set up a small office locally.
本部の意見は来週にならないと出てこない。: Headquarters won't give its opinion until next week.
